belief: If a teaching makes me feel good, it must be from God.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that if a teaching makes you feel good it must be from God, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Popular preaching that focuses mainly on comfort, success, and self-improvement. Past hurt from harsh teaching, which makes any challenge feel unsafe. Wanting God’s Word to always encourage and never correct. Social media and books that sound spiritual but are mostly positive thinking. Confusing emotional uplift with spiritual truth.
teaches: God’s Word does bring comfort, hope, and joy. But Scripture also warns that people will gather teachers who say what their itching ears want to hear. God’s Word is living and active and sometimes cuts deeply, correcting us for our good. A friend’s honest wounds can be more faithful than an enemy’s kisses. The test of a teaching is whether it is true to Scripture, not whether it makes us feel good.
self_statements: That sermon felt great, so it must be true.
God would never say anything that makes me uncomfortable.
If a teaching challenges me, it must be wrong.
Real Christianity always makes you feel good.
I only listen to teachers who encourage me.
errors: Judging a teaching by how it feels rather than by Scripture.
Accepting comforting verses and avoiding challenging ones.
Believing truth must be either all comfort or all harshness.
Seeking out only teachers who confirm what you want.
questions: What does 2 Timothy 4:3–4 say about teachers who suit our desires?
Does God’s Word ever correct or challenge me?
Is this teaching true to all of Scripture, or just to the parts I like?
Have I ever needed a hard truth that didn’t feel good at first?
Am I avoiding a message because it’s wrong, or because it’s uncomfortable?
What does Hebrews 4:12 say God’s Word does?
Can truth be loving and still be hard to hear?
truth: A teaching is not from God just because it makes me feel good. God’s Word brings comfort, but it also corrects and challenges me for my good. I can test every teaching by Scripture, receive both encouragement and correction, and trust that God’s truth is always loving, even when it is hard.
hw_questions: What does Paul say about teachers who suit our desires?
Does God’s Word ever correct me?
Is this teaching true to all of Scripture?
Have I needed a hard truth before?
Am I avoiding this because it’s wrong or uncomfortable?
Can truth be loving and still hard to hear?
hw_truths: I test teaching by Scripture, not by feelings.
God’s Word comforts me and corrects me.
Hard truths can be loving truths.
God’s Word is living and active.
I want truth, not just comfort.
The wounds of a friend are faithful.
log: After each sermon, video, or book, write: What did it say? How did it feel? Is it true to Scripture?
name_example: All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for instruction, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness, so that Sarah may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.
actions: Pick a teacher you enjoy and check one message
against Scripture, writing down any verses that confirm or challenge it.
Read a passage of Scripture that challenges you,
such as Matthew 5:21–48, and write one area where God is correcting you.
Ask a trusted Christian friend for honest feedback
on one area of your life, and thank them for it.
that even the devil quoted Scripture to sound right.
prayer: Father, thank You for the comfort of Your Word and for the correction it brings. Help me reject the lie that a teaching must be from You if it makes me feel good. Give me a love for Your truth, even when it is hard, and wisdom to test everything by Your Word. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
